deed: צהל מקים בית חולים שדה בנפאל — ומטפל באלף וארבע מאות פצועים
title: The IDF set up a field hospital in Kathmandu after the earthquake in Nepal and treated more than a thousand patients

trailer.text: Israel's medical delegation to Nepal was, as of the time it was sent, the 24th delegation Israel had sent to 22 countries in the 30 years before it.
According to the Times of Israel, a magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck Nepal and killed at least 5,000 people.
The Israeli team left on Monday morning, two days after the quake of Saturday, April 25.
In Kathmandu, in the Nepali army's compound, it set up a field hospital.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the hospital treated more than 1,000 patients, and at the closing ceremony a Nepali minister expressed his government's gratitude to Israel.

glance.label: When
glance.value: According to the Jerusalem Post, the field hospital operated for 10 days and was shipped back to Israel on Sunday, 10 May 2015.

glance.label: Where
glance.value: Kathmandu, in the Nepali army's compound

glance.label: Scope
glance.value: More than 1,000 patients, according to the Jerusalem Post

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: The thanks of the Nepali government at the closing ceremony

paragraphs.text: According to the Times of Israel, the earthquake was of magnitude 7.8.
According to the report, it left thousands dead and wounded.
The partial collapse of Nepal's largest private orphanage left 100 children homeless.
The children suffered from severe diarrhea.
At the time of the earthquake there were 2,000 Israelis in Nepal.
According to the report, only one of them remained unaccounted for.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Israelis helped locate Or Asraf, the only Israeli backpacker who died in an avalanche during the quake.

Colonel Dr. Tarif Bader, who commanded and oversaw the IDF delegation to Nepal in 2015, was presented, at the time the source was written, as the Deputy Surgeon General of the Israel Defense Forces Medical Corps.
According to Hadassah Magazine, on Monday morning, two days after the disaster, a 747 airplane took off from Tel Aviv.
On board were physicians, surgeons, nurses and other medical staff.
The Israelis came from nearly 5,000 kilometers away, and yet they were among the fastest to arrive.
According to Merin, the Nepalese feared that the weight of the plane would damage the runway, the only one that was usable in the area.
In the end they approved the landing.
More than 250 doctors and rescue personnel landed on Tuesday in Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal.
According to the IDF, this was the largest delegation the IDF had ever sent abroad.
The cost, several million shekels, was shared by the Finance Ministry and the IDF.
According to Prof. Jonathan Halevy, the team left with an equipped tent hospital.
It had X-ray machines, generators, respirators and computerized medical record systems.
The hospital had operating rooms, imaging, advanced laboratories and an intensive care unit.
The operating rooms could treat three patients at the same time.
The IDF brought powdered plasma, an Israeli invention that allows blood stocks to be kept indefinitely in areas without refrigeration, where they would otherwise spoil.
The hospital included an obstetrics department and operated in coordination with the local army hospital.
There was no running water, and members of the delegation improvised toilets using pits they had dug.
The hospital also had a synagogue and a kosher kitchen.
Communication with Israel was by satellite and local phones, and in the first week there was no internet.
According to the IDF Spokesperson, the hospital began operating on Wednesday morning and treated nearly 100 patients that same day.
Among the patients on the first day were some 30 Israelis, most of them with dehydration, and they were quickly released to their hotels.
According to Dr. Ofer Merin, medical director of the IDF field hospital, one type of patient was those who had been trapped for up to four days and had been air evacuated to Kathmandu.
Trekkers who had been stuck in the mountains also arrived, many of them with frostbite and more serious injuries.
Pemba Tamang, 15, was trapped for five days under the rubble of the guesthouse where he worked as a bellboy.
Prof. Amos Peizer said that the team saw many open fractures and had to perform amputations.
Dr. Uri Ilan had no dialysis equipment, so he performed manual dialysis following instructions from Hadassah by satellite phone.
Padova said that the team paid for an ambulance that took a girl to the Israeli hospital, where she underwent brain surgery and is recovering.
About a third of the patients were children, and some of them were orphans.
According to Bader, many wounded were transferred from local hospitals to the Israeli hospital to continue complex treatment.
According to the Jerusalem Post, most of the teams could not speak with the wounded, because few locals spoke English.
According to the IDF Spokesperson, on the first day the hospital delivered its first baby.
Midwife Michal Peres was on the team that delivered it.
The hospital became the preferred hospital for some of the injured, and some pregnant women came to it to give birth.
According to the Jerusalem Post, of the 1,600 patients, including 80 with very serious injuries, only three died.
According to an article in Prehospital and Disaster Medicine, 31% of the patients were hospitalized, and the most common operation was wound debridement.
The Home Front Command checked the stability of 332 public buildings and held 605 safety courses for the Nepalese public.
According to Hadassah Magazine, Nepal's Prime Minister Sushil Koirala attended the opening of the hospital.
According to Bader, soon after the arrival, senior government and health officials began making pilgrimages to the hospital.
At a small closing ceremony, Nepal's Urban Development Minister, Narayan Khadka, expressed his government's gratitude to Israel.
Halevy said that he did not think about the risk of another earthquake.
Such an earthquake, of magnitude 7.3, did come soon after the team left.
The medical director was Lt. Col. (res.) Dr. Ofer Merin, a senior cardiothoracic surgeon and trauma expert, and deputy director-general of Shaare Zedek Medical Center in Jerusalem.
Merin said that Jewish tradition regards saving one life as saving a whole world.
He said that the local doctors received the Israelis with open arms and that the joint work with them was unique.
Dr. Hagit Padova, head of the IDF medical branch, led her first mission to a disaster zone.
She had feared she would miss it, because she keeps Shabbat.
Padova said that Israel has a humanitarian responsibility and a moral obligation to save lives.
Many on the medical team were not religious Jews, and it included at least one Druze.
Hundreds of Israeli backpackers came to the hospital to help, among them a trained physiotherapist.
The Nepali physician Dr. Kshichwa served two weeks at the field hospital and treated some 200 casualties.
Three days after the opening, the medical clowns of the Dream Doctors Project arrived.

claims.text: המשלחת הרפואית לנפאל היא ה-24 ש-ישראל שלחה ל-22 מדינות ב-30 השנים האחרונות.
claims.quote: Israel’s medical delegation to Nepal is the 24th it has sent to 22 countries in the past 30 years.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, רעידת האדמה בעוצמה 7.8 הרגה לפחות 5,000 בני אדם והותירה כ-8,000 פצועים.
claims.quote: magnitude-7.8 earthquake that devastated large swaths of the mountainous country, killing at least 5,000 and leaving some 8,000 wounded

claims.text: הצוות יצא ביום שני בבוקר.
claims.quote: The team left on Monday morning, less than 30 hours after learning of the quake.

claims.text: בית החולים בן 60 המיטות הוקם בקטמנדו במתחם הצבא הנפאלי, לאחר רעידה שלפי הדיווח הרגה למעלה מ-7,900 איש ופצעה יותר מ-16,000.
claims.quote: The 60-bed field hospital was based in the Nepali capital, Kathmandu, in its army's cantonment compound following the earthquake that killed over 7,900 people and injured more than 16,000.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, בית החולים השדה הישראלי טיפל ביותר מ-1,000 מטופלים במהלך 10 ימי פעילותו.
claims.quote: Israel's field hospital treated over 1,000 patients during its 10 days of operation

claims.text: בטקס קטן לסיום הפעילות הביע שר הפיתוח העירוני של נפאל, נראיין חאדקה, את הכרת תודתה של ממשלתו לישראל.
claims.quote: At a small function to mark the closure of the emergency aid facility, Nepal's Urban Development Minister Narayan Khadka expressed his government's gratitude to Israel for its help.

claims.text: למעלה מ-250 רופאים ואנשי חילוץ במשלחת צה"ל נחתו ביום שלישי בקטמנדו, בירת נפאל.
claims.quote: Over 250 doctors and rescue personnel were part of an IDF delegation that landed Tuesday in the Nepalese capital, Kathmandu

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, בין 26 באפריל ל-13 במאי טיפל הצוות הרפואי הישראלי בן 122 האנשים ב-1,600 מטופלים, ביצע 90 ניתוחים מצילי חיים ויילד שמונה תינוקות, ששה מהם בניתוח קיסרי.
claims.quote: Between April 26 and May 13, the 122-member Israeli medical team treated 1,600 patients, performed 90 lifesaving operations and delivered eight babies (including six by cesarean section).

claims.text: קריסה חלקית של בית היתומים הפרטי הגדול בנפאל הותירה 100 ילדים ללא בית ועם שלשול קשה.
claims.quote: The partial collapse of Nepal’s largest private orphanage, Bal Mandir, had left 100 children homeless and suffering severe diarrhea.

claims.text: מבין 2,000 הישראלים שהיו בנפאל בזמן הרעידה, אחד בלבד נותר חסר עקבות לפי הדיווח.
claims.quote: Of 2,000 Israelis who were in the country when the natural disaster hit, only one remains unaccounted for

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, ישראלים אלה עזרו לאתר את אור אסרף, המטייל הישראלי היחיד שמת במפולת שלגים במהלך הרעידה.
claims.quote: It was these Israelis who helped locate Or Asraf, the one Israeli backpacker who died in an avalanche during the quake.

claims.text: אל"מ ד"ר טריף בדר הוא סגן קצין הרפואה הראשי של חיל הרפואה בצה"ל.
claims.quote: Colonel Dr. Tarif Bader is the Deputy Surgeon General of the Israel Defense Forces Medical Corps.

claims.text: לפי Hadassah Magazine, ביום שני בבוקר המריא מטוס 747 מתל אביב עם 260 רופאים, מנתחים, אחיות ואנשי צוות רפואי נוספים.
claims.quote: On Monday morning, 30 hours after the catastrophe, a 747 airplane left Tel Aviv carrying 260 physicians, surgeons, nurses, X-ray technicians, paramedics, psychologists and physiotherapists.

claims.text: הצוות הישראלי הגיע בין המהירים ביותר, אף שבא ממרחק של כמעט 5,000 קילומטר.
claims.quote: It was also among the speediest to arrive, even though the team came from nearly 5,000 kilometers away

claims.text: לפי מרין, הנפאלים חששו שמשקל המטוס יגרום נזק למסלול, היחיד שהיה שמיש באזור, ובסוף אישרו את הנחיתה.
claims.quote: were afraid that the weight would cause damage to the runway – the only one that was usable in the area.

claims.text: לפי צה"ל, בית החולים בנפאל הוא המשלחת הגדולה ביותר שנשלחה אי פעם על ידי צה"ל לחו"ל.
claims.quote: The IDF noted that the hospital operating in Nepal is the largest delegation ever deployed overseas.

claims.text: העלות, כמה מיליוני שקלים, חולקה בין משרד האוצר לצה"ל.
claims.quote: The cost of several million shekels was shared by the Treasury and the IDF.

claims.text: לפי פרופ' ג'ונתן הלוי, הצוות יצא עם בית חולים אוהלים מאובזר, מכשירי רנטגן, גנרטורים, מכונות הנשמה ומערכות רשומה רפואית ממוחשבת.
claims.quote: We left less than 30 hours after being called – with a fully equipped tent hospital, x-ray machines, electric generators, respirators, computerized medical record systems

claims.text: בבית החולים היו חדרי ניתוח, הדמיה, מעבדות מתקדמות ויחידת טיפול נמרץ, ו-150 ישראלים טיפלו במטופלים.
claims.quote: The hospital offered operating rooms, imaging facilities, advanced labs and an intensive care section with 150 Israelis taking care of its patients.

claims.text: במתקן היו חדרי ניתוח מתקדמים המסוגלים לטפל בשלושה מטופלים בו-זמנית, מעבדות, ציוד אבחון ומערכות מעקב אחר מטופלים.
claims.quote: The facility features advanced operating rooms capable of treating up to three patients at a time and all necessary laboratories, diagnostic equipment and patient tracking systems.

claims.text: צה"ל הביא פלזמה אבקתית, המצאה ישראלית שמאפשרת מלאי בלתי מוגבל של דם באזורים ללא קירור.
claims.quote: The IDF also brought powered plasma, an Israeli invention that allows indefinite stockpiles of blood that would otherwise perish in areas lacking in refrigeration.

claims.text: הקבוצה הישראלית הקימה בית חולים שדה עם 60 מיטות, כולל מחלקת מיילדות, ופעלה בתיאום עם בית החולים של הצבא המקומי.
claims.quote: The Israeli group set up the field hospital with 60 beds, including an obstetrics department, and was operating in coordination with the local army hospital.

claims.text: בבית החולים השדה לא היו מים זורמים, ואנשי המשלחת אלתרו שירותים באמצעות חפירת בורות.
claims.quote: אין מים זורמים בנמצא, ואנשי המשלחת אלתרו תאי שירותים על ידי חפירת בורות

claims.text: בבית החולים הייתה גם בית כנסת ומטבח כשר.
claims.quote: It also had a synagogue and a kosher kitchen.

claims.text: הקשר עם ישראל נעשה בטלפונים לוויניים ומקומיים, ולא היה חיבור לאינטרנט במשך השבוע הראשון.
claims.quote: Communication with Israel was made possible with satellite and local phones; there was no Internet connection during the first week.

claims.text: לפי דובר צה"ל, בית החולים השדה הישראלי בנפאל החל לפעול ביום רביעי בבוקר, טיפל בכמעט 100 מטופלים ויילד את התינוק הראשון שלו.
claims.quote: Israel’s field hospital in earthquake-hit Nepal began operating Wednesday morning, with staff treating nearly 100 patients and delivering their first baby

claims.text: בין המטופלים ביום הראשון היו כ-30 ישראלים, שרובם סבלו מהתייבשות ושוחררו במהירות למלונותיהם.
claims.quote: Among the patients were some 30 Israeli nationals. Most were suffering from dehydration and were soon released to their hotels.

claims.quote: Those who had been trapped for up to four days that had just been air evacuated to Kathmandu.

claims.quote: Trekkers stuck in the mountains, many of them suffering frostbite and more extensive wounds.

claims.quote: One of them was 15-year-old Pemba Tamang, who had been trapped for five days under the rubble of the guesthouse where he was a bellboy.

claims.quote: We saw a lot of open fractures with bones exposed, and we had to do amputations.

claims.text: ד"ר אורי אילן, בהיעדר ציוד דיאליזה, הפעיל דיאליזה ידנית לפי הנחיות מהדסה בטלפון לווייני.
claims.quote: Introducing himself as “today’s resident in charge at the tent hospital in Nepal,” he followed Dr. Braun’s manual dialysis directions.

claims.quote: We paid for an ambulance to take her to the Israeli hospital, she had neurosurgery and she's getting better.

claims.text: כשליש מהמטופלים היו ילדים, חלקם יתומים.
claims.quote: About a third of the patients were children, some of whom had lost their parents.

claims.quote: Many of the wounded were evacuated from local hospitals and transported to our facilities to continue receiving necessary and complex care.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, רוב הצוותים הרפואיים לא יכלו לתקשר עם הפצועים והחולים כי מעט מקומיים דיברו אנגלית.
claims.quote: in most cases the medical teams couldn't communicate with the wounded and sick because few locals spoke English.

claims.quote: שהיתה אתמול בצוות שיילד את התינוק הראשון במוסד הרפואי המאולתר

claims.text: בית החולים הפך לבית החולים המועדף על חלק מהפצועים, וחלק מהנשים ההרות הגיעו אליו ללדת.
claims.quote: During the period it became the preferred hospital for some of the injured to come for treatment and some pregnant mothers came to deliver their babies.

claims.quote: Of all the 1,600 treated, including 80 with very serious injuries, “just” three died.

claims.quote: The hospitalization rate was 31%. Wound debridement procedures were the most common operations performed.

claims.text: פיקוד העורף סרק 332 מבנים ציבוריים לבדיקת יציבותם והעביר 605 קורסי בטיחות לציבור הנפאלי.
claims.quote: The IDF Home Front Command scanned 332 public buildings to check whether they were still stable, and held 605 safely courses for the Nepalese general public.

claims.text: לפי Hadassah Magazine, בית החולים היה מבצעי תוך 12 שעות מהנחיתה, ובפתיחתו נכח ראש ממשלת נפאל סושיל קוירלה.
claims.quote: The State of Israel IDF Medical Corps Hospital was operational within 12 hours of landing, its launch attended by Nepal’s Prime Minister Sushil Koirala

claims.quote: Soon after our arrival, our hospital became a pilgrimage site for senior government and healthcare officials.

claims.quote: that there might be another earthquake [which there in fact was, with a 7.3 magnitude] soon after the team left Nepal.

claims.quote: Ofer Merin, a senior cardiothoracic surgeon and trauma expert who is deputy director-general of Jerusalem's Shaare Zedek Medical Center.

claims.quote: As head of the army's medical branch, the lieutenant colonel was leading her first mission to a disaster zone, having feared she had missed her chance because she kept Shabbat.

claims.quote: We don't ask why, because Israel has a humanitarian responsibility, a moral obligation to save lives.

claims.quote: Many of the members of the medical team were not religiously observant Jews; there was at least one Druse.

claims.text: הרופא הנפאלי ד"ר קשיצ'ווה שירת שבועיים בבית החולים השדה וטיפל בכ-200 נפגעים.
claims.quote: He spent two weeks at the IDF field hospital, treating some 200 quake victims.

claims.text: שלושה ימים אחרי פתיחת בית החולים הגיעו ליצחק הליצנים הרפואיים מטעם פרויקט רופאי החלום.
claims.quote: Three days after Israel opened its field hospital, the therapeutic clowns showed up, courtesy of the Dream Doctors Project.

claims.text: לפי ה-Jewish Chronicle, במשך שבועיים טיפלו הצוותים ב-1,700 נפגעים, ביצעו יותר מ-200 ניתוחים ויילדו שמונה תינוקות.
claims.quote: Over the next two weeks, teams worked round the clock finding and treating 1,700 victims, performing more than 200 operations and delivering eight babies.

claims.text: לפי בדר, הצוות טיפל ביותר מ-1,600 פצועים וחולים במהלך השהות בנפאל.
claims.quote: We cared for more than 1,600 injured and sick patients throughout our stay in Nepal

claims.text: לפי המאמר, הצוות כלל 42 רופאים וטיפל בסך הכול ב-1,668 מטופלים.
claims.quote: The EMT staff was comprised of 42 physicians. A total of 1,668 patients were treated.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, הצוות הרפואי ביצע 85 ניתוחים בפצועים אזרחים נפאליים.
claims.quote: The hospital's medical personnel carried out 85 operations on injured Nepalese civilians.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, נולדו בבית החולים שמונה תינוקות, מהם שניים בניתוח קיסרי.
claims.quote: Eight babies were born in it, including two births requiring cesarean section operations.

claims.text: בדר כתב שבמהלך השהות בנפאל יילד הצוות שישה תינוקות.
claims.quote: During our stay in Nepal we had the privilege of delivering and welcoming six babies into the world.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, בית החולים השדה של צה"ל היה הגדול ביותר, עם 260 איש ובהם 45 רופאים.
claims.quote: Not only was the Israel Defense Forces' field hospital by far the largest, with 260 people, including 45 physicians and with nurses, x-ray technicians and more.

claims.text: לפי וואלה, משלחת צה"ל לנפאל מנתה 269 אנשי צוות, ובהם רופאים, מחלצים, אחיות ופרמדיקים.
claims.quote: משלחת צה"ל לנפאל מונה 269 אנשי צוות, ובהם רופאים, מחלצים, אחיות, פרמדיקים, חובשים קרביים ולוחמים, וכן אנשי לוגיסטיקה.

claims.text: לפי Defense News, יחידה רפואית ישראלית בת 260 איש דיווחה על טיפול בכ-100 נפגעים עד ליל רביעי, פחות מ-12 שעות אחרי פריסת בית החולים.
claims.quote: A 260-strong Israeli medical unit reports having treated some 100 victims of the Nepalese earthquake by Wednesday night, Nepal time

claims.text: לפי ד"ר טריף בדר, 82 שעות אחרי הרעידה היה בית החולים השדה מוכן בקטמנדו.
claims.quote: Eighty-two hours after the earthquake struck, we were ready with a field hospital deployed in the capital, Kathmandu.

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-Prehospital and Disaster Medicine, הצוות הרפואי הישראלי נפרס 80 שעות אחרי הרעידה.
claims.quote: The Israeli Emergency Medical Team (IEMT; later verified as EMT-3) was deployed 80 hours after the earthquake.

claims.text: המטען, 95 טון, כלל בית חולים שדה בן 80 מיטות עם שני חדרי ניתוח וארבעה חדרי טיפול נמרץ.
claims.quote: Its 95-ton cargo included an 80-bed field hospital with two operating rooms and four intensive-care rooms

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, בית החולים השדה נשלח חזרה לישראל ביום ראשון לאחר סיום המשימה.
claims.quote: The IDF field hospital in Nepal was shipped off for Israel on Sunday after its humanitarian mission was completed in the earthquake-stricken country.

claims.text: לפי Hadassah Magazine, הישראלים השאירו את בית החולים השדה שלהם לנפאלים.
claims.quote: They left their field hospital behind for the stricken Nepalese.

claims.text: היחידה נתמכה ב-100 טון ציוד ואספקה והייתה מוכנה לטפל במאות מטופלים נוספים בימים הקרובים.
claims.quote: Supported by 100 tons of equipment and supplies, the unit is prepared to treat hundreds more patients over the coming days

claims.text: סין, השנייה בגודל משלחתה, שלחה רק 37 אנשי מקצוע ויפן ארבעה.
claims.quote: China, the next largest, sent only 37 professionals, and Japan four.

claims.text: 260 אנשי צה"ל, יותר מכל מדינה אחרת מלבד הודו, נחתו 48 שעות אחרי האסון.
claims.quote: 260 IDF personnel - more than from any other country apart from India - touched down 48 hours after

claims.text: לפי CNN, כפי שמצוטט ב-Hadassah Magazine, שיירת הסיוע הישראלית הייתה גדולה מכל מאמצי הסיוע האחרים לנפאל יחד.
claims.quote: Israel’s aid convoy was, according to CNN, larger than all other aid efforts to Nepal combined.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, בית החולים השדה של צה"ל בנפאל נשלח חזרה לישראל ביום ראשון, אחרי שפעל 10 ימים.
claims.quote: The IDF field hospital in Nepal was shipped off for Israel on Sunday ... It was in operation for 10 days.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, מטוס הסיוע של צה"ל המריא מנמל התעופה בן גוריון לנפאל ביום שני בבוקר.
claims.quote: lifted off from Ben Gurion Airport Monday morning for earthquake-battered Nepal

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, הרעידה אירעה בשבת, 25 באפריל, והצוות יצא ביום שני בבוקר.
claims.quote: on Shabbat, April 25, soon after the earthquake occurred ... The team left on Monday morning

sources.label: Times of Israel Blogs, Tarif Bader, 2016

quote_translations.c70: who was yesterday on the team that delivered the first baby at the improvised medical facility
quote_translations.c68: The IDF delegation to Nepal numbers 269 staff members, among them doctors, rescuers, nurses, paramedics, combat medics and soldiers, as well as logistics personnel.
